ModelCharacter: A larger traditional Albin Taiwan trawler with two private cabins, full walkaround decks, teak-rich interior and well-protected running gear, providing liveaboard-scale comfort while retaining economical semi-displacement cruising.
DesignLineage: The Albin 40 Trawler was produced from 1987–1993.

ModelVariations.Name: Long production and hull-family evolution
ModelVariations.Description: C-Dory model names span multiple production eras. The 26 Pro Angler is a documented historical model; the current TomCat is the 25-foot TomCat 255, not a current 30-foot model.

ModelCharacter: A rare wide-walkaround C-Dory fishing model from the brand's earlier experimental period, using a narrower pilothouse and a 12-degree bottom to create safer foredeck access and a much larger working cockpit than the conventional Cruisers. Both inboard and bracketed-outboard examples exist.
DesignLineage: Owner records verify surviving C-Dory 26 Pro Anglers from the 1980s through at least 2005, but production appears to have been very limited.
The cabin is approximately the width of a C-Dory 22 cabin but longer, leaving true walkaround side decks.
The model is not the same hull/design as the later 26 Venture; C-Brats owner history describes the Venture as a descendant of the Cape Cruiser line.
Because factory documentation is sparse and propulsion varied between inboard and outboard, B-Atlas retains the Pro Angler as a separate model at Moderate confidence.
OwnershipCharacter: A highly individual boat rather than a standardized pocket cruiser. Walkaround access is excellent for anchoring and fishing, but propulsion, transom arrangement, cabin fitout and overall weight vary enough that each hull must be evaluated from survey and HIN rather than generic specs.

ModelCharacter: The benchmark Grand Banks: a two-stateroom aft-cabin cruiser with full walkaround decks, substantial teak interior and enough size for extended living without crossing fully into large-yacht scale. Its long production run made it the reference point for the entire traditional trawler category.
DesignLineage: The 42 Classic became one of Grand Banks' longest-running and highest-production Heritage models.

The 42 Europa and 42 Motor Yacht share the broader 42-family platform but use different deckhouse and aft-deck arrangements.

ModelCharacter: The working-boat expression of the Rosborough 246: a trailerable Nova Scotia-derived wheelhouse cruiser with 360-degree visibility, sliding pilot doors and a large open cockpit. It is equally credible as a fishing, patrol, search-and-rescue or minimalist cruising platform.
DesignLineage: Bob Rosborough developed the first fiberglass RF-246 after experimenting with several earlier designs; the first 246 was delivered in 1987.
The Custom Wheelhouse is the utility-oriented branch of the same proven 25-foot RF-246 hull family.
Rosborough built nearly 500 examples over roughly 25 years before selling the molds to Eastern Boats in New Hampshire.
Eastern Boat Works continues the Rosborough 246 hull today, with the Custom Wheelhouse retained alongside more cruising-focused Yarmouth, Halifax and Digby layouts.
OwnershipCharacter: Rugged, simple and highly adaptable. Outboard versions are particularly easy to service, while older boats may have diesel inboard or sterndrive power; sparse interior trim and commercial-style construction generally reduce cosmetic maintenance compared with yachtier pocket cruisers.

Strengths: Large flybridge for size

ModelVariations.Description: Current XL 2400 production is documented with outboard power; older 24-foot Sea Sports may use different propulsion and should not be assumed identical.

ModelCharacter: A modern Pacific Northwest deep-V pilothouse fishing/cruising boat with a deliberately shorter cabin and longer cockpit than the Explorer 2400. At 24 feet and 8'6" beam it remains trailerable, but its 22-degree deadrise, 5,000-pound hull and large fuel supply make it far more offshore-oriented than a C-Dory.
DesignLineage: The XL 2400 and Explorer 2400 share Sea Sport's 24-foot deep-V platform.
The XL uses a shorter 5'10" cabin and 8'8" cockpit to prioritize fishing and deck work.
The Explorer stretches the cabin to 8'3" and reduces cockpit length for more cruising accommodation.
Current boats use outboard propulsion, reflecting Sea Sport's evolution away from earlier sterndrive-heavy configurations.
OwnershipCharacter: Robust but not lightweight: deep-V hull, 149 gallons of fuel and single/twin outboards create significantly higher towing and operating demands than flatter pocket cruisers. Current builder support and outboard serviceability are strong positives.
